Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 1–4:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Anfal (ال​أنفال): plural of nafl (with a fatha on the fa'), meaning what the leader (imam) gives to individual members of the army as encouragement.

Dhat bbaynikum (ذات بينكم): that is, the reality of your relations with one another. Al-bayn is the bond and tie that links you to one another through affection and brotherhood.

Innama al-mu'minun (إنما المؤمنون): that is, those who are perfect in their faith.

Wajilat qulubuhum (وجلت قلوبهم): that is, their hearts feared. Al-wajal is fear, especially at the mention of His threat and His promise.

Wa 'ala rabbihim yatawakkalun (وعلى ربهم يتوكلون): they rely upon Allah alone and entrust their affairs to Him alone.

Wa mimma razaqnahum (ومما رزقناهم): that is, what We gave them.

Ulaika (أولئك): that is, those described by the five qualities mentioned above.

Lahum darajat (لهم درجات): high ranks in Paradise.

Wa rizq karim (ورزق كريم): that is, a great bounty of every kind of blessing in Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

These verses were revealed concerning the Battle of Badr. The Prophet (ﷺ) had given a share of the spoils (nafl) to some of the fighters for their valour, while others who had not taken part were left out. Disputes arose among the fighters: why was this one given and why was that one not? They asked the Messenger (ﷺ), and Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾. He informed them that they belong ﴿to Allah and the Messenger﴾: Allah judges concerning them as He wills, and the Messenger distributes them among you as his Lord commands him. Therefore, ﴿fear Allah﴾, the Exalted, by abandoning dispute and discord, ﴿and set right what is between you﴾ by strengthening the bonds of love among you and purifying your hearts of every rancour or hatred that arose from these spoils and your disagreement over dividing them. ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾ in everything they command you and forbid you, ﴿if you are believers﴾ truly; so carry out the command and avoid what is forbidden.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿The believers are only those﴾: that is, those who are perfect in their faith, who deserve this description, the believers, are ﴿those whom, when Allah is mentioned﴾, that is, His name, His promise, or His threat, ﴿their hearts become fearful﴾, that is, they fear and so refrain from disobedience and hasten to obedience. ﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾: that is, their faith grows strong and their certainty becomes great. ﴿And upon their Lord﴾, not upon anyone else, ﴿they rely﴾; and in Him, the Exalted, they trust, and to Him they entrust their affairs. ﴿Who establish prayer﴾ by performing it with all its conditions, all its pillars, and all its recommended practices and etiquette. ﴿And from what We have provided them﴾, that is, what We have given them, ﴿they spend﴾ from wealth, knowledge, status, and bodily health; from all of these they spend in the way of Allah. ﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾, those described by these five qualities, ﴿for them are degrees with their Lord﴾: that is, high ranks, varying in height and elevation, in Paradise. And before that they have ﴿forgiveness﴾, complete, for their sins, ﴿and noble provision﴾: good, abundant sustenance with no deficiency or turbidity in it, and that is in Paradise, the abode of the righteous.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The command to fear Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to set right what is between people.

2- Faith increases through obedience and decreases through disobedience.

3- Among the believers are those whose faith is complete, and among them are those whose faith is deficient.

4- Among the qualities of those of complete faith is what is mentioned in the second verse of this surah and what follows it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 5–8:

Explanation of the words:

"From your house" (min baytika): i.e., Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah.

"Averse" (la-karihun): i.e., to going out to fight.

"One of the two groups" (iḥdā al-ṭā'ifatayn): the caravan (al-'Ir), or the army (al-Nafir): the army of Quraysh and its troops.

"Might" (al-shawkah): weapons in war.

"Nullifies falsehood" (yubṭil al-bāṭil): i.e., makes its falsehood manifest by subduing its people, breaking their might and defeating them.

"Though the criminals dislike it" (wa-law kariha al-mujrimūn): the disbelieving, polytheist Quraysh.

The meaning of the verses:

His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿As your Lord brought you out﴾ O Messenger, ﴿from your house﴾ in al-Madinah, ﴿in truth﴾, clothed in it, since you went out by the permission of Allah. ﴿And indeed, a group of the believers were averse﴾ when they learned that Quraysh had come out to fight them, and the outcome was a great good. This situation is like their situation when they disliked the seizing of the spoils from their hands and the dividing of them by Our permission, in the most just, most sound and most beneficial division. So this statement in this verse [5] contains a comparison of the situation of the present with the situation of the past; in each of them there occurred the aversion of some of the believers, and in each the outcome was good, and praise be to Allah.

His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿They argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾, i.e., they argue with you about fighting after it had become clear to them that the caravan had escaped and that only the army remained, and that fighting it was unavoidable.

His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿as though they were being driven toward death while they watch﴾, i.e., toward death, seen with their own eyes, witnessing it before them, and this was from the intensity of their aversion to a fight for which they had not prepared and for which they had not steeled themselves to plunge into its battles.

His statement, Exalted is He, ﴿And [recall] when Allah promised you one of the two groups﴾, i.e., O Messenger, mention to them the time when Allah promised you one of the two groups, the caravan or the army; this was both in Al-Madinah and during the march. ﴿That it would be yours﴾, i.e., you would triumph over it. ﴿And you wished﴾, i.e., you loved, that it be ﴿the one without might﴾, which was the caravan of Abu Sufyan, ﴿to be yours﴾, because it was spoil without cost, given the paucity of its numbers and its equipment. But Allah wanted ﴿to establish the truth﴾, i.e., to make it manifest by the victory of His allies and the defeat of His enemies. His statement ﴿by His words﴾, i.e., those which include His command to you to fight the disbelievers, and His command to the angels to fight alongside you. His statement ﴿and cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾, i.e., by empowering you over them so that you kill them, until none of them remains except one who flees and escapes. His statement ﴿that He might establish the truth﴾, i.e., that He might support it and confirm it, and it is Islam; ﴿and nullify falsehood﴾, and it is polytheism; ﴿even though the criminals dislike it﴾, i.e., the polytheists, who committed crimes against themselves by corrupting them with polytheism, and against others as well, in that they prevented them from accepting Islam and turned them away from it by every means.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the principle of ﴿But it may be that you dislike a thing and it is good for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216], and mentioning an overview of the Battle of Badr al-Kubra. The explanation: the Prophet ﷺ received word that a caravan of Quraysh carrying merchandise was coming from Syria on its way to Makkah, headed by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. So the Prophet ﷺ dispatched some of his companions to go out toward it, perhaps Allah would grant them its spoils, because Quraysh had confiscated the property of some of them, and some had left their wealth in Makkah and emigrated. When the Prophet ﷺ set out, and during his journey, he informed them that Allah had promised them one of the two groups, not specifically: it was possible that it was the caravan, and it was possible that it was the army that had come out from Makkah to defend the caravan and to repel the Messenger and his companions from it, so that they would not seize it. When the Messenger received news of the caravan's escape and the army's approach, he consulted his companions; they agreed to fight the polytheists at Badr, while some of them disliked that and said: "We had not prepared for fighting." So Allah revealed these verses: ﴿They argue with you concerning the truth after it has become clear﴾ up to His statement {... though the criminals dislike it}.

2- Clarifying the weakness of human beings in their desire for everything that involves no cost and no hardship.

3- The fulfillment by Allah of His promise to the believers, in that He granted them the spoils of the army's group and honored them with a victory for which they had not been prepared.

4- Mention of an overview of the Battle of Badr, which is among the most famous and most excellent of battles, and whose participants were among the best and most excellent of the Companions, since it took place in a time of the Muslims' weakness, when it occurred in the second year of the Hijrah, while they were a minority and all the Arabs were their enemies and opponents.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*Tastaghithun* (you seek relief): you ask God Most High for help, which is victory over your enemies.

*Murdifin* (following one another): coming in succession, one after another.

*Wa ma ja'alahu Allah illa bushra* (God did not make it except as good news): the reinforcement with angels was only good news for you of victory.

*Idh yughashikumu al-nu'as* (when He covers you with drowsiness): He covers you with it. *Al-nu'as* is a very light sleep.

*Amanatan* (as security): safety from the fear that had afflicted you because of your small number and the large number of your enemy.

*Minhu* (from Him): from God Most High.

*Rijz al-shaytan* (the defilement of Satan): his whispering to you, with that which pains and grieves you.

*Wa liyarbita 'ala qulubikum* (and to bind your hearts): to strengthen them with patience and certainty.

*Wa yuthabbita bihi al-aqdam* (and to make your feet firm thereby): that is, by the rain, your feet are made firm so that they do not sink into the sand.

*Al-ru'b* (terror): fear and alarm.

*Fadribu kulla banan* (so strike every fingertip): that is, the extremities of the hands and feet, so that they are prevented from striking and walking.

*Shaqqu Allah wa rasulahu* (they opposed God and His Messenger): they defied His purpose for them and did not obey Him, and they opposed His Messenger.

*Dhalikum fadhuquhu* (that, so taste it): that is, the punishment; so taste it.

*Adhab al-nar* (the punishment of the Fire): that is, in the Hereafter.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

The context still concerns the events of the Battle of Badr (*ghazwat Badr*), and the clarification of God's favours upon His Messenger and the believers. God Most High says to His Messenger ﴿When you sought help from your Lord﴾, meaning: remember, O Our Messenger, your condition when you were fearful because of your small number and the large number of your enemy, so you sought help from your Lord, saying: "O God, grant us victory; O God, fulfil for me what You have promised me." ﴿So He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ That is, coming in succession, one after another. ﴿God did not make it except as good news﴾, meaning that this reinforcement was merely good news for you of victory over your enemy. ﴿And so that your hearts might be reassured thereby﴾, meaning that they might be calmed and that anxiety and agitation might depart from them. As for victory, it is from God alone. ﴿Indeed, God is Mighty and Wise﴾: Mighty, Overpowering, such that nothing can stand between Him and what He wills; Wise, in granting victory to one who is worthy of it. This is one blessing.

Second: remember ﴿when He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾, meaning a security from God Most High for you. When drowsiness overcomes a servant, he becomes calm and tranquil, and fear departs from him, and he stands firm on the battlefield, neither fleeing, nor dreading, nor retreating. ﴿And He sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby and to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾. This is another blessing. The ground was sandy, and their feet sank into it, so they could neither advance nor retreat with ease. Their water had become scarce, so they were thirsty and parched, in a state of ritual impurity, finding neither water to drink nor water with which to purify themselves from their states of impurity. Satan whispered to some of them with words such as: "You fight in a state of impurity; how can you be victorious? You fight while you are thirsty, and your enemy is well watered," and other such whisperings. So God Most High sent down, upon their camp in particular, abundant rain. They drank and purified themselves, and the soil was packed by it, so that it became suitable for fighting upon. This is the meaning of God's words ﴿And He sent down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby and to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾, that is, his whispering. ﴿And to bind your hearts﴾, that is, to strengthen them with the patience He poured upon them and the certainty He placed within them. ﴿And to make your feet firm thereby.﴾ Another blessing. Remember ﴿when your Lord revealed to the angels: "I am with you"﴾, by My support and My victory, ﴿so strengthen those who believe﴾, that is, say to them words of encouragement that will make them steadfast in battle. ﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾, that is, fear, O believers. ﴿So strike above the necks﴾, that is, strike the necks. ﴿And strike from them every fingertip﴾, that is, the extremities of the hands and feet, so that they can neither strike with the sword nor flee on foot. God's words ﴿That is because they opposed God and His Messenger﴾ mean that they showed enmity towards them and fought against them. ﴿And whoever opposes God and His Messenger﴾, He will avenge himself upon him and seize him, ﴿for indeed God is severe in punishment.﴾ God's words ﴿That, so taste it﴾ mean: that punishment, namely killing and defeat, so taste it in this world. As for the Hereafter, for you there is the punishment of the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Jazā'irī (Aysar al-Tafāsīr) on Surah 8, verses 15–19**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Zaḥfan* (زحفاً): advancing toward one another, meaning they approach slowly because of their large numbers, as if they were crawling along the ground.

*Fa-lā tuwallūhumu al-adbār* (فلا تولوهم الأدبار): do not flee in defeat before them, so that you turn your backs to them.

*Mutaḥarrifan li-qitāl* (متحرفاً لقتال): one who shifts from one side to another in order to be able to strike the enemy and fight him.

*Aw mutaḥayyizan ilā fi'ah* (أو متحيزاً إلى فئة): one who seeks to join a group of believers that will fight alongside him.

*Faqad bā'a bi-ghaḍab* (فقد باء بغضب): he returned from the battle accompanied by anger from God, because he disobeyed Him.

*Wa-liyubliya* (وليبلي): so that He may bestow upon them the blessing of victory and triumph despite their small number, that they may give thanks.

*Fi'atakum* (فئتكم): your fighting force, made up of your many men.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The discussion continues concerning the Battle of Badr and the great blessings and hidden wisdom contained in it. In the first of these verses, the Lord, blessed and exalted, addresses His believing servants and says: ﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing (for battle)...﴾, meaning while you and they are advancing toward one another. ﴿...then do not turn your backs to them﴾, meaning do not be routed before them so that you give them your backs and enable them to kill you. You are more deserving of victory and more entitled to triumph and dominance, for you are believers and they are disbelievers, so it is never proper for you to be routed. ﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾, except ﴿one who shifts (position) for battle﴾, meaning one who moves from one side to another so that this will be more effective for him in fighting, ﴿or one who withdraws to a company﴾, meaning one who joins a group of believers that fights, so that he fights with them to strengthen them or to be strengthened by them. Whoever turns his back to the disbelievers in other than these two situations ﴿has indeed returned with anger from God﴾, meaning he came back from his struggle accompanied by the anger of God. ﴿And his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination﴾, and this is after his death and his transfer to the Hereafter.

God's words ﴿So you did not kill them, but God killed them﴾ inform His believing servants, to whom turning away at the moment of advancing was forbidden, and whom He threatened with His anger and the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, that they did not in reality kill the polytheists; rather, it was God who killed them. He is the One who commanded them, empowered them, and assisted them. Had it not been for Him, no one would have been killed or died. Let them know this so that it does not occur to them that they alone were the ones who fought. And as for the throwing by His Messenger of the handful of dust at the polytheists, which reached the eyes of the polytheists in the battle, bewildering and confounding them, and even preventing them from fighting and causing their defeat, it was God, exalted be He, who was the Thrower, who caused the dust to reach the eyes of the polytheists. For had the Messenger ﷺ been left to his own strength, the handful of dust would not have reached the eyes of the front rank of the polytheist fighters. Therefore God said: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw﴾. God's words ﴿and that He might bestow upon the believers a good favor from Him﴾ mean that God did all that killing, throwing, and delivering of dust into their eyes in order to humble the disbelievers and break their power, ﴿and that He might bestow upon the believers﴾, meaning that He might grant them a fine blessing by giving them victory and support in this world and admitting them to Paradise in the Hereafter.

God's words ﴿Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾: by virtue of these two attributes came the fine bestowal. He, exalted be He, heard the words of the believers and their pleas to Him, and knew their weakness and need, so He supported them and gave them victory, and this was from Him a fine bestowal. God's words ﴿That is so, and [know that] God weakens the plot of the disbelievers﴾ mean that this killing, throwing, and bestowal all constitute a truth that comes to pass by the power of God, exalted be He. ﴿And [that] God weakens﴾, meaning makes feeble, ﴿the plot of the disbelievers﴾. Whenever they plot against His allies and the people of His obedience, He weakens it and nullifies its effect. To Him belong praise and grace.

God's words ﴿If you seek a decision, there has certainly come to you the decision; and if you cease, it is better for you﴾ are addressed to the polytheists, when Abū Jahl and other leaders of the polytheists said: "O God, whichever of us is more wicked toward You and more severing of the ties of kinship, then destroy him this day. O God, cut off the one of us who severs ties of kinship the most, and bring us that which we do not know, so destroy him in the morning." That is, destroy him in the morning of the day of Badr. So God, exalted be He, revealed: ﴿If you seek a decision﴾, meaning you seek the decision, which is the judgment between you and our Prophet Muḥammad, ﴿there has certainly come to you the decision﴾, which is their defeat at Badr. ﴿And if you cease﴾, that is, you refrain from war and fighting and submit to the judgment of God, exalted be He, so that you are safe, ﴿it is better for you﴾. ﴿And if you return﴾ to war and disbelief, ﴿We will return﴾, so We will give power over you to Our Messenger and the believers, that We may make you taste humiliation and defeat at their hands. ﴿And your company will not avail you at all, even if it is numerous﴾, and even if the number of your fighting men reaches tens of thousands. This is because God is always with the believers, and He will never abandon their support and aid so long as they remain upright in obedience to their Lord, outwardly and inwardly.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The prohibition of fleeing from the disbelieving enemy at the moment of encounter, given the anger and punishment God has threatened for it, and because the Messenger ﷺ counted it among the seven destructive sins in the hadith of Muslim: "and fleeing on the day of the battle line."

2. Affirmation of the principle that God is the Creator of everything, that He created the servant and created his act. Since the servant is created, his power is created, and he is commanded and forbidden, and no act or word proceeds from him except by God's empowerment, the true Agent is God. The servant has only the acquisition (*kasb*) through his limbs, and by this reward is given for good with good and for evil with its like. This reflects God's justice and mercy.

3. The sign of the dust from the palm of the Messenger ﷺ reaching most of the eyes of the polytheists in the battle.

4. The honor of God and His fine bestowal upon His allies, so to Him belong praise and grace.

5. God's guardianship of the sincere believers is the means of their victory, perfection, and happiness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 20–23:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And do not turn away from Him﴾: i.e., do not turn away from obeying Him when He commands you or forbids you, as if you do not hear.

﴿Indeed, the worst of living beings﴾: i.e., the worst of what crawls upon the earth are the disbelievers.

﴿That He would have made them hear﴾: i.e., that He would have made them hear, or removed the obstacle from them so they would hear and respond.

The meaning of the verses:

God, exalted is He, calls out to His servant believers, those who believed in Him and His Messenger and affirmed His promise and threat on the Day of meeting Him. He commands them to obey Him and to obey His Messenger, and forbids them from turning away from Him while they hear the verses recited and the admonitions following one another in the Book of God and on the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Your victory and support were the fruit of your faith and obedience. So if you turn away and disobey, abandoning every guardianship of God over you, you become like others among the people of disbelief and disobedience. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, obey God and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him while you hear.﴾ And His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear.﴾ He, Mighty and Majestic, forbids them from taking the path of the disbelieving polytheists in being deaf to hearing the verses that carry the truth and call to it, and in being blind to seeing the signs of God that indicate His oneness. These are those who said, "We are, regarding what Muhammad says, deaf, and regarding what he mentions and points to, blind." They say, "We hear with our ears," but they do not hear with their hearts, because they do not reflect or think. Therefore, in their hearing they are like one who has not heard, since what counts is hearing that benefits, not merely hearing a sound.

And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living beings in the sight of God are the deaf, the dumb, who do not reason.﴾ By this He means the polytheists, who were the worst of living beings because they disbelieved in their Lord, associated partners with Him, worshipped other than Him, and strayed from His way, and so they transgressed, did wrong, and committed crimes. This is what made them truly the worst of living beings upon the earth. This is a condemnation of the polytheists and at the same time a warning to the believers against disobeying God and His Messenger and turning away from His Book and the guidance of His Prophet (ﷺ).

And His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear.﴾ That is, He would have made them hear the verses of God and what they carry of good news and warning. This is by way of supposition, based on His saying: ﴿And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being averse.﴾ These are a group of polytheists who plunged deep into evil, corruption, wrongdoing, arrogance, and obstinacy, and so they were deprived of God's guidance. Some of them perished at Badr and some at Uhud without believing, because God knew there was no good in them. And how could it not be so, when He is their Creator and the Creator of their natures? ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾ [al-Mulk: 14].

Lessons from the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- The obligation to obey God and His Messenger in their commands and prohibitions, and the prohibition of disobeying them.

2- The prohibition of imitating the polytheists, disbelievers, and all people of misguidance, in every aspect of their conduct.

3- A declaration that among people there are those worse than dogs and pigs, let alone camels, cattle, and sheep; those are a group who disbelieved and wronged, and God would not forgive them nor guide them to a path.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 24–26:

Explanation of the words:

*Istajibu*: listen and obey.

*Li-ma yuhyikum*: that is, to that which is the source of your life and that which is a cause of your life, such as faith, righteous deeds and jihad.

*Fitnah*: that is, a punishment by which you are tested, such as famine, sickness, or the domination of an enemy.

*Mustad'afun*: that is, weak before your enemies; they see you as weak and so they inflict harm upon you.

*Wa-razaqakum min al-tayyibat*: the plural of *tayyib*, meaning all the lawful (*muhallal*) things, including food, drink and other things.

*La'allakum tashkurun*: in the hope that you will thank Him, the Exalted, by spending the blessing in that which pleases Him.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the third call of honour to the believers. The Lord, exalted is He, honours them by calling them, so that He may ennoble them with what He commands them or forbids them, as an upbringing for them and a preparation for them for the happiness and honour of both abodes. So He says: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾. This has the same meaning as the first call: obey Allah and His Messenger. His saying ﴿to that which gives you life﴾ indicates that the commands of Allah and His Messenger, like their prohibitions, are never free of that which gives life to the believers, increases their life, or preserves it for them; therefore it is obligatory to obey Allah and His Messenger as far as obedience to them is possible. His saying ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a person and his heart﴾ is a great warning to the believers: when an opportunity for good presents itself to them, they should seize it before it is lost, especially if it is a call from Allah or His Messenger, because Allah, the Exalted, is able to intervene between a person and what he desires, and between a person and his heart, so that He turns the heart and directs it to another direction, in which it dislikes good and desires evil. His saying ﴿and that to Him you will be gathered﴾: one who knows that he will be gathered to Allah, the Exalted, whether he likes it or not, how can his intellect permit him to hear His call to His command or prohibition and then turn away from it? His saying ﴿And beware of a trial which will not afflict those among you who have wronged exclusively﴾ is another great warning to the believers not to abandon obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and to abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil; then evil spreads and corruption becomes general, and affliction descends, encompassing the righteous and the wicked, the pious and the sinful, the oppressor and the just. His saying ﴿And know that Allah is severe in punishment﴾ is an affirmation of the warning: when He punishes for sin and disobedience, His punishment is harsh and severe, unbearable, so let the believers guard against this by adhering to obedience to Allah and His Messenger. The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people would snatch you away, but He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help and provided you with good things, that you might be grateful﴾. This is a divine admonition to those believers who lived with the Islamic call from its early days. Their Lord reminds them of their previous state of fewness and weakness, when they feared that people would snatch them away because of their fewness and weakness; then the Mighty and Majestic sheltered them in the illuminated city of His Prophet and aided them with His soldiers, so they became mighty after humiliation and became rich after poverty and need. He provided them with good things, of food, drink, clothing and mounts; He provided them with good things as an honour to them, to prepare them thereby for gratitude, since the one who lives in and wears a blessing is the one who is thankful for it. Gratitude is praising the Benefactor, extolling Him, obeying Him, loving Him, and spending the blessing in the way that pleases Him. Allah knows that they were grateful; may Allah be pleased with them and make them pleased, and join us to them as patient and grateful ones.

Guidance from the verses:

1- It is obligatory to respond to the call of Allah and His Messenger by doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, because of what that brings of life to the Muslim individual.

2- It is required to seize the opportunity for good before it is lost; whenever it presents itself to the believer, it is incumbent upon him to seize it.

3- It is obligatory to enjoin good and forbid evil, as protection against general trials in which the just and the unjust perish alike.

4- It is obligatory to remember blessings in order to be grateful for them, by obeying Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.

5- It is obligatory to thank for blessings by praising Allah, extolling Him, acknowledging the blessing as coming from Him, and using it in accordance with His pleasure.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 27–29:

Explanation of the words:

*Do not betray Allah and the Messenger* (لا تخونوا الله والرسول): that is, by displaying faith and obedience while opposing them inwardly.

*Nor betray your trusts* (وتخونوا أماناتكم): that is, do not betray the trusts that some of you place with one another.

*Your wealth and your children are only a trial* (إنما أموالكم وأولادكم فتنة): that is, being occupied with them tempts you away from obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

*If you fear Allah* (إن تتقوا الله): that is, by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition in belief, speech and action.

*He will grant you a criterion* (يجعل لكم فرقاناً): a light in your insight by which you distinguish between the beneficial and the harmful, and the righteous and the corrupt.

*And will remove from you your misdeeds* (ويكفر عنكم سيآتكم): that is, He will erase from you what has passed of your sins that lie between you and Him.

*And will forgive you* (ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم): that is, He will cover them, concealing them from you so that He does not expose you through them nor hold you accountable for them.

The meanings of the verses:

This is another divine address directed to the believers: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, O you who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Muhammad as Messenger, and in Islam as religion. ﴿Do not betray Allah and the Messenger﴾ by one of you displaying obedience to Allah and His Messenger while concealing disobedience, and do not betray your trusts that some of you place with others ﴿while you know﴾ the gravity of the crime of betrayal and its evil effects on the self and society. This is what the first verse in this context indicates: ﴿O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts while you know.﴾ His statement, exalted is He, ﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward﴾ contains an allusion to the cause that most often drives to betrayal, which is wealth and children. So He, exalted is He, informed them that their wealth and children are a trial that diverts them from trust and obedience, and that whatever one hopes for from wealth or offspring is nothing compared to what is with Allah, for with Allah is a great reward for whoever obeys Him, fears Him, and guards his trust with Allah, His Messenger, and the servants of Allah. His statement, exalted is He, in the third verse: ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you﴾ is an exhortation to piety and an encouragement toward it, by mentioning its greatest outcomes: first, the granting of the criterion, which is victory and the decisive separation between every ambiguity, and the distinguishing between truth and falsehood, the harmful and the beneficial, the sound and the corrupt; second, the removal of misdeeds; third, the forgiveness of sins; and fourth, the great reward, which is Paradise and its bliss. He said, exalted is He, at the end of the verse: ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾, an allusion to what Allah gives the people of piety in the Hereafter, which is Paradise, and His good pleasure upon its people. How excellent is the reward for which workers work.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The prohibition of betrayal in all its forms, the worst of which is betrayal of Allah and His Messenger.
2. Wealth and children are a trial that may lead to betraying Allah and His Messenger, so the believer should beware of it.
3. Among the fruits of piety are the removal of misdeeds and the forgiveness of sins, and the criterion, which is a light in the heart by which the pious person distinguishes between matters that are ambiguous and in which the face of truth and good is hidden.

He said, exalted is He, at the end of the verse: ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾, an allusion to what Allah gives the people of piety in the Hereafter, which is Paradise, and His good pleasure upon its people. How excellent is the reward for which workers work.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The prohibition of betrayal in all its forms, the worst of which is betrayal of Allah and His Messenger.
2. Wealth and children are a trial that may lead to betraying Allah and His Messenger, so the believer should beware of it.
3. Among the fruits of piety are the removal of misdeeds and the forgiveness of sins, and the criterion, which is a light in the heart by which the pious person distinguishes between matters that are ambiguous and in which the face of truth and good is hidden.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 30–31:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa idh yamkuru bika* (And when they plotted against you): i.e., they planned against you what would harm you.

*Liyuthbitūka* (to imprison you): i.e., to confine you, bound fast, so that you could not escape from confinement.

*Aw yukhrijūka* (or drive you out): i.e., to banish you far from their homes.

*Wa yamkurūna wa yamkuru Allāh* (They plot, and Allah plots): i.e., they arrange evil for you and devise harm against you, and Allah, exalted is He, also arranges for them what will harm them and devises for them what will distress them.

*Āyātunā* (Our verses): the verses of the Noble Qur'an.

*Asāṭīr al-awwalīn* (tales of the ancients): asāṭīr is the plural of usṭūra, meaning what is written down and inscribed of the reports of the ancients.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, reminds His Messenger and the believers of one of His blessings upon them, saying to His Messenger: "And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you, [to imprison you, or kill you, or drive you out]" (8:30). This refers to when the Quraysh gathered in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house), conferred about the matter of the Prophet ﷺ, schemed and plotted, and issued a decision to kill him ﷺ, and sent someone to carry out the crime of killing. They surrounded his house, but the Prophet ﷺ went out after he had thrown a handful of dust at them, saying, "May your faces be disfigured," and no one saw him; he got away and emigrated to Madinah. This is the meaning of "And they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters" (8:30). Thus, his ﷺ deliverance from the hand of the Quraysh was a great blessing upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and upon all the believers. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in the second verse: "And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is not but tales of the ancients'" (8:31). This report is a denunciation of the stance of the polytheists, mentioned after the mention of their base conspiracies and their wicked plotting, where they resolved to kill him ﷺ. Allah, exalted is He, informs that when the Messenger recites to them the verses of Allah, which make the truth clear and establish faith in Him and His messengership, by mentioning the stories of the ancients, they say, "We have heard" what you recite to us; "If we willed, we could say the like of this," i.e., what you say; "This is not but tales of the ancients," i.e., the reports of earlier nations, written down and inscribed, which are dictated to you so that you memorize them and recite them to us. The speaker of this false statement was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, may the curses of Allah be upon him, who died in disbelief.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Reminding of the blessings of Allah upon the servant, so that the servant finds in himself the impulse to give thanks and thus gives thanks.

2- Demonstrating the extent to which the Quraysh opposed the call of Islam, to the point that they issued their ruling to kill the Messenger ﷺ.

3- Clarifying the stance of the polytheists toward the Islamic call, and that they expended every effort to end it and eliminate it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 32–35:

Explanation of the words:

Allahumma (O Allah): the yā' of the vocative has been dropped from the beginning, and the mīm at the end has been added in its place.

In kāna hādhā (if this is): i.e., that which Muhammad brought and reports.

Fa-amtir (then rain down): send down upon us stones.

Yasuddūna ʿan al-Masjid al-Ḥarām (they bar people from the Sacred Mosque): they prevent people from entering it for ʿumrah.

Muka' wa-tasdiyah: al-muka' is whistling, and al-tasdiyah is clapping.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to condemn some of the statements and deeds of the polytheists. This is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, who said in the preceding verses, ﴿Had we willed, we could have said the like of this. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients﴾ [al-Anfal: 31]. Allah, exalted is He, tells us that he said, ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿so that we are destroyed by them, and we do not see Muhammad victorious with his religion among us. ﴿Or bring us a painful punishment﴾, so that we are rid of our existence. Then Allah, exalted is He, said, ﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them﴾, for your presence among them is a security for them. ﴿Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, since when they used to circumambulate, some of them would say, "Forgive us, our Lord, forgive us." Then Allah, exalted is He, said, ﴿And what is [wrong] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām﴾, i.e., what prevents the punishment from them while they commit the most abominable crime, which is barring people from entering the Sacred Mosque to circumambulate the Sacred House. They used to prevent the believers from circumambulating the House and from praying in the Sacred Mosque. His statement, exalted is He, ﴿And they were not its guardians﴾, is a refutation of their claims that they were the custodians of the Sacred Precinct and those in charge of it, and therefore they had the right to prevent whomever they wished and permit whomever they wished. So Allah, exalted is He, said in response to them, ﴿And they were not its guardians﴾, i.e., guardians of the Sacred Mosque, just as they were not the friends of Allah either. The friends of Allah and of the Sacred Mosque are only the God-fearing, who guard against polytheism and sins. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾. This is due to the ignorance of some of them and the obstinacy of others. As for His statement, ﴿And their prayer at the House was not but whistling and clapping﴾, it refers to the fact that when some of them circumambulated, they would clap and whistle, as some proponents of Sufism do, dancing while clapping and whistling, and they regard this as the assembly of the friends of Allah. We seek refuge with Allah from ignorance and misguidance. His statement, exalted is He, ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾, refers to what He made them taste on the Day of Badr, when He humiliated and disgraced them in it and killed their leaders.

Guidance from the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification of the state of the polytheists of Makkah, their hatred of the truth and their aversion to it, to the extent that they asked for a general punishment rather than see the banner of truth raised and the religion of Allah victorious.

2- The Prophet ﷺ is a security for his ummah from punishment, so this ummah was not struck by the punishment of total annihilation and complete destruction.

3- The virtue of seeking forgiveness, and that it saves from the punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

4- Clarification of the great sin of one who bars people from the Sacred Mosque from performing the lawful worship in it.

5- Clarification of the friends of Allah, exalted is He, who are entitled to be in charge of the Sacred Mosque, namely the God-fearing.

6- Disapproval of whistling and clapping, and the invalidity of dancing in worship.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafsir) on Surah 8, verses 36–37:

Explanation of the words:

Inna alladhina kafaru (Indeed, those who disbelieve): i.e., those who denied the signs of Allah and the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ) from among the Quraysh.

Thumma takunu alayhim hasratan (Then it will be a regret for them): i.e., intense remorse.

Thumma yughlabun (Then they will be defeated): i.e., they will be routed.

Liyamiza (That He may distinguish): i.e., that He may separate each category from the other.

Al-khabith (the wicked): they are the people of polytheism and sins.

Min al-tayyib (from the good): they are the people of monotheism and righteous deeds.

Fayarkumahu (and heap it up): i.e., He will make some of it upon others in Hell.

Meaning of the noble verses:

The context continues in censure of the polytheists and their losing deeds. Allah, exalted is He, informs: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾, and they are the people of Makkah among the leaders of Quraysh, ﴿spend their wealth﴾ in war against the Messenger of Allah and the believers, to bar people from Islam, which is expressed as the Way of Allah. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So they will spend it; then it will be a regret for them﴾, i.e., intense remorse because of the evil outcome that befell them at Badr, Uhud and the Trench, when they spent on these three campaigns from wealth of which Allah is knowing. Then they failed in them and lost, and consequently they were defeated, their disbelieving authority ended, and Allah granted His Messenger and the believers the conquest of Makkah. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., whoever of them died upon disbelief, ﴿to Hell they will be gathered﴾, i.e., they will be assembled. The reason for this gathering is that Allah, exalted is He, distinguishes the wicked from the good. The good, who are the righteous believers, cross the Bridge to the Garden, the abode of bliss. As for the wicked, who are the group of polytheists, He places some of them upon others and heaps them all together in one heap, and casts them into Hell. And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Those are the losers﴾ refers to those who spent their wealth to bar from the way of Allah and died upon disbelief, were gathered to Hell, had some of them placed upon others, then were made into one heap, and then were cast into the Fire of Hell. They are truly the losers, for they lost themselves, their wealth, their families and everything, and they became in the depths of Hell, despairing. We seek refuge with Allah from manifest loss.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Every expenditure that a servant makes to bar people from the way of Allah, in whatever manner, will be a great regret upon him on the Day of Resurrection.

2- Every disbeliever and every believer is good.

3- The truth of Allah's promise to His Messenger and the believers of the defeat and conquest of the polytheists, and their regret over what they spent in fighting Islam, and the loss of all that and their failure in it.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 8, verses 41–44:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Anna mā ghanimtum min shay'* (whatever you take as spoils of war): That is, whatever you seize from the property of the disbelievers by force and domination, whether little or much.

*Fa-inna lillāhi khumusahu* (then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it): That is, one-fifth of the five divisions, which belongs to Allah, the Messenger, and those mentioned after them.

*Wa-li-dhī al-qurbā* (and to the near of kin): These are the relatives of the Messenger ﷺ from Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib.

*Wa-mā anzalnā ʿalā ʿabdinā* (and what We sent down upon Our servant): That is, of the angels and the signs.

*Yawm al-furqān* (the Day of Criterion): That is, the Day of Badr, which fell on the seventeenth of Ramadan, when Allah distinguished therein between truth and falsehood.

*Iltaqā al-jamʿān* (the two hosts met): The host of the believers and the host of the disbelievers at Badr.

*Al-ʿudwat al-dunyā* (the near bank): *al-ʿudwa* is the edge of a valley and its side; *al-dunyā* means the nearer one, close to Madinah.

*Bil-ʿudwat al-quṣwā* (the far bank): That is, the one farther from Madinah, since it was the edge of the valley on the other side.

*Wa-l-rakbu asfala minkum* (and the caravan was lower than you): That is, the caravan of Abu Sufyan, which was the trade caravan they had set out to meet. "Lower than you" means on the side nearer the sea.

*ʿan bayyinah* (on clear evidence): That is, a manifest proof.

*Latanāzaʿtum fī l-amr* (you would have disputed the matter): That is, you would have differed.

*Wa-yuqallilukum fī aʿyunihim* (and He made you appear few in their eyes): This was before the engagement; after it, they saw them as twice their number, so that the defeat was completed for them.

**Meaning of the verses:**

There is no doubt that these verses were revealed to explain the division of the spoils after a dispute had arisen over them. Allah took them out of their hands and then divided them among them. He had said, "The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger" at the beginning of the verse, and now He says, **"And know"** O Muslims, **"that whatever you take as spoils of war,"** even a thread or a needle, the meaning of *ghanimtum* being that you seized it as property from the hands of the disbelievers who fought you, by domination and force over them. Its division is that **"one-fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer."** The remaining four-fifths are yours, O fighters: a foot soldier receives one share, and a horseman receives two shares, because of his effect in battle and because his horse requires provision of fodder. What is meant by Allah's share is that it is spent on public interests; it would be more fitting to spend it on His houses, namely the Kaʿbah and all the mosques. What is for the Messenger he spends on his family. What is for the near of kin is spent on the relatives of the Messenger who are forbidden to take zakat because of their nobility, namely Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib. What is for the orphans is spent on the poor Muslims. What is for the wayfarer is spent on travelers cut off from their homelands, when they are in need during their journey.

His saying, **"If you have believed in Allah,"** that is, as Lord, **"and in what We sent down upon Our servant,"** that is, Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, **"on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met,"** which is the day of Badr, when the Muslims met the polytheists. What is meant by what Allah sent down upon His servant and Messenger is the angels and the signs, among them the handful of dust he threw at the polytheists, which reached most of them and caused their defeat.

His saying, **"And Allah is over all things competent,"** that is, just as He was able to grant you victory despite your small number, and was able to defeat your enemy despite their great number, He is capable of everything He wills.

His saying, **"When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side, and the caravan was lower than you,"** is a reminder to them of the battlefield, in which the signs of Allah became manifest and His favor upon them appeared, so that they might prepare themselves to be thankful.

His saying, **"Even if you had made an appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment,"** that is, if you and the polytheists had agreed upon a meeting at Badr for battle, you would have differed, for reasons that would call for that, among them that you were few and they were many. **"But that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed,"** that is, determined by Allah's decree and destiny, namely your victory and the defeat of your enemy, and your gathering without prior appointment or previous agreement.

His saying, **"That whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence,"** this is the cause of Allah's act of bringing you together in the valley of Badr for battle. He did so that whoever would live by faith might live upon evidence and knowledge that Allah is true, Islam is true, the Messenger is true, and the Hereafter is true, since Allah showed them the signs indicating that. And whoever would perish through disbelief might perish upon evidence, since it became clear to him that what the polytheists held was disbelief, falsehood, and error, yet he still approved of it and persisted in it.

His saying, **"And indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing,"** is an affirmation of what preceded and an emphasis upon it, since He informs that He hears the words of His servants and knows their deeds. What He reported and affirmed is as He reported and affirmed.

His saying, **"When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few,"** that is, you informed your companions, and they rejoiced at that and were gladdened and prepared themselves for battle. And His saying, **"Had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage, and you would have disputed about the matter of fighting,"** that is, you would have become cowardly about fighting them. **"But Allah saved [you] from that,"** so He did not show them to you as many. Indeed He, exalted, knows what is in the breasts, and He did that because of His knowledge of what would result from it of good and evil.

His saying, **"And when He showed them to you as few in your eyes,"** that is, remember, O believers, when Allah showed you the disbelievers at the time of your meeting with them as few in your eyes, as if they were seventy men or a hundred, and He, glorified and exalted, made you appear few in their eyes so that they would not fear you. This was at the time of confrontation and before the engagement. After the engagement, Allah showed the disbelievers the believers as double their number, as came in Surah Al ʿImran in His saying, **"They saw them as twice their number"** [Verse: 13]. And His saying, **"That Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed,"** is the cause of those divine arrangements for His allies, to grant them victory and honor and to humble and degrade their enemies. And His saying, **"And to Allah are all matters returned,"** is information from Him, exalted, that all matters return to Him, so whatever He wills of them comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be, whether it is a report or something else.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation of the division of the spoils in the manner that Allah, exalted, is pleased with.
2. A reminder of faith, for it is the directing force, given that the believer is alive through his faith and is able to act and to refrain, while the disbeliever is dead and is not held accountable.
3. The virtue of the Battle of Badr and the merit of its participants.
4. Explanation of Allah's arrangement in granting victory to His allies and defeat to His enemies.
5. Explanation that the outcome of matters, whether success or failure, belongs to Allah, exalted; no one has any influence in them except by His permission.

*Latanāzaʿtum fī l-amr* (you would have disputed the matter): That is, you would have differed.

*Wa-yuqallilukum fī aʿyunihim* (and He made you appear few in their eyes): This was before the engagement; after it, they saw them as twice their number, so that the defeat was completed for them.

**Meaning of the verses:**

There is no doubt that these verses were revealed to explain the division of the spoils after a dispute had arisen over them. Allah took them out of their hands and then divided them among them. He had said, "The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger" at the beginning of the verse, and now He says, **"And know"** O Muslims, **"that whatever you take as spoils of war,"** even a thread or a needle, the meaning of *ghanimtum* being that you seized it as property from the hands of the disbelievers who fought you, by domination and force over them. Its division is that **"one-fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer."** The remaining four-fifths are yours, O fighters: a foot soldier receives one share, and a horseman receives two shares, because of his effect in battle and because his horse requires provision of fodder. What is meant by Allah's share is that it is spent on public interests; it would be more fitting to spend it on His houses, namely the Kaʿbah and all the mosques. What is for the Messenger he spends on his family. What is for the near of kin is spent on the relatives of the Messenger who are forbidden to take zakat because of their nobility, namely Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib. What is for the orphans is spent on the poor Muslims. What is for the wayfarer is spent on travelers cut off from their homelands, when they are in need during their journey.

What is meant by what Allah sent down upon His servant and Messenger is the angels and the signs, among them the handful of dust he threw at the polytheists, which reached most of them and caused their defeat.

His saying, **"And Allah is over all things competent,"** that is, just as He was able to grant you victory despite your small number, and was able to defeat your enemy despite their great number, He is capable of everything He wills.

His saying, **"When you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side, and the caravan was lower than you,"** is a reminder to them of the battlefield, in which the signs of Allah became manifest and His favor upon them appeared, so that they might prepare themselves to be thankful.

His saying, **"Even if you had made an appointment, you would have differed concerning the appointment,"** that is, if you and the polytheists had agreed upon a meeting at Badr for battle, you would have differed, for reasons that would call for that, among them that you were few and they were many. **"But that Allah might accomplish a matter already decreed,"** that is, determined by Allah's decree and destiny, namely your victory and the defeat of your enemy, and your gathering without prior appointment or previous agreement.

His saying, **"That whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence,"** this is the cause of Allah's act of bringing you together in the valley of Badr for battle. He did so that whoever would live by faith might live upon evidence and knowledge that Allah is true, Islam is true, the Messenger is true, and the Hereafter is true, since Allah showed them the signs indicating that. And whoever would perish through disbelief might perish upon evidence, since it became clear to him that what the polytheists held was disbelief, falsehood, and error, yet he still approved of it and persisted in it.

1. Explanation of the division of the spoils in the manner that Allah, exalted, is pleased with.

3. The virtue of the Battle of Badr and the merit of its participants.
4. Explanation of Allah's arrangement in granting victory to His allies and defeat to His enemies.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 45–49:

Explanation of the words:

Fi'ah (fi'a): a fighting group.

Fathbutu: stand firm for fighting it and hold your ground.

Wadhkuru Allah kathiran: glorifying Allah (tahlil), magnifying Him (takbir), hoping for victory, aspiring to it, and asking Allah Most High for it.

Tuflihun: you will succeed with victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter, after being saved from defeat in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter.

Wa la tanaza'u: that is, do not differ with one another while you face the enemy, not at any time.

Wa tadhhaba rihukum: that is, your strength, because of disagreement.

Kharaju min diyarihim bataran: that is, out of arrogance (batar), which is rejecting the truth and refusing it.

Wa qala inni jarun lakum: that is, I am a protector (mujir) for you and a helper against your enemy.

Tara'a'ati al-fi'atan: that is, the two groups met and each saw its enemy.

Nakasa 'ala 'aqibayh: that is, he turned back fleeing backward, because he had come to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik.

Inni ara ma la tarawn: [referring to] the angels.

Wa alladhina fi qulubihim maradh: that is, weakness in their faith and a flaw in their creed.

Meaning of the verses:

This noble address is directed to the believers, who were given permission to fight the disbelievers. It began with the expedition of ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with him, and was followed by this campaign, the great Battle of Badr. Therefore they were in need of divine instruction and heavenly guidance, by which they would know how to conduct battles and achieve victory in them. In these four verses there is a very lofty instruction for conducting battles and gaining victory in them. The following is its explanation:

1- Steadfastness in the face of the enemy and perseverance in fighting, to the point that the mujahidin are like a towering mountain that does not move: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company, stand firm﴾, that is, a fighting group, ﴿fathbutu﴾.

2- The remembrance of Allah Most High through tahlil, takbir, tasbih, supplication, humility, promise and warning. ﴿And remember Allah often that you may succeed﴾, that is, that you may win victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter, after being saved from defeat and humiliation in this world, and from the Fire and punishment in the Hereafter.

3- Obedience to Allah and His Messenger in their commands and prohibitions, and among this is obedience to the commander and director of the battle, and this is among the greatest factors of victory according to the sunnah of Allah Most High in the universe: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾.

4- Non-dispute and non-disagreement during the planning of the battle, at its beginning, and during its conduct.

5- Clarification of the consequences of dispute and disagreement, which are: utter failure, and the loss of strength, expressed by "wind": ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart﴾.

6- Patience in continuing the fighting and preparing for it, and disciplining the soul and readying it for that: ﴿And be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾.

7- Sincerity in fighting and going out for it for the sake of Allah Most High, so that no consideration other than seeking the pleasure of Allah should be present: ﴿And do not be like those who went out from their homes in arrogance and to be seen by people, and who averted [others] from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾.

These are the factors of victory and the conditions of jihad in the way of Allah. Three of these five verses included them, and His saying in the fourth verse [48]: ﴿And [remember] when Satan made their deeds attractive to them and said, "No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your protector." But when the two forces sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment."﴾ Allah Most High reminds the believers of an event that occurred on the day of Badr, one of the most strange events, to be a lesson and admonition for the believers. So He, Mighty and Majestic, says: remember when Satan made attractive to the polytheists, whom I forbade you to imitate in their conduct, their fighting, and their whole life, and he said to them: advance to fight Muhammad and the believers, and do not fear or be afraid, for there is no one among the people who can overcome you today, and I am your protector, meaning I am your protector, supporter and helper.

At that hour, Satan was in the form of a man of the nobles of his tribe called Suraqah ibn Malik. When the two groups saw each other and advanced to fight, Satan saw Gabriel among the ranks of the angels, so he turned back on his heels. He had been holding the hand of al-Harith ibn Hisham, speaking to him, promising him and giving him hopes, after he had made the battle attractive to them and encouraged them to it. He turned and fled, so al-Harith said to him, "What is wrong with you? What has befallen you? Come back!" He said, while fleeing: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment﴾. He spoke the truth, though he is a liar.

His saying at the end of the verse [49]: ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say, "Their religion has deluded these"﴾, that is, remember, O believers, for lesson and admonition, when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease, meaning weakness in faith and instability in belief, say: "Their religion has deluded these." Otherwise they would not have gone out to fight Quraysh, who outnumbered them in men and equipment. Such words are considered commonplace from the weak in faith and the hypocrites who conceal their false faith. So remember this, and let such words not weaken your resolve. Rely upon Allah, confident in His support, for He will support you, because He is Mighty, never overcome nor prevented from what He wills, and Wise, who places victory with those qualified for it through faith, patience, obedience to Him and to His Messenger, and sincerity to Him in deed and obedience.

Guidance from the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification of the causes and factors of victory and the obligation to adopt them in every battle, which are: steadfastness, remembrance of Allah Most High, obedience to Allah and His Messenger, obedience to leadership, avoidance of dispute and disagreement, patience, and sincerity.

2- Clarification of the factors of failure and loss, which are: dispute, disagreement, arrogance, showing off, and self-deception.

3- Clarification of Satan's work in the souls of the disbelievers through his making war attractive to them, his promises, and his giving them false hopes.

4- Clarification of the condition of the hypocrites and the weak in faith when fighting exists and wars break out.

5- The obligation to rely upon Allah and depend on Him, whatever the claims of the falsifiers, the discouragers, and the defeatists.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 50–54:

Explanation of the words:

*Idh yatawaffa* (when they take them in death): that is, they seize their souls to cause their death.

*Wujuhahum wa adbarahum* (their faces and their backs): that is, they strike them from in front of them and from behind them.

*Bi-zallamin lil-'abid* (not a wrongdoer to the servants): that is, He is not one who wrongs His servants, like His saying ﴿And your Lord wrongs no one﴾ [al-Kahf: 49].

*Ka-da'bi Al Fir'awn* (like the custom of the folk of Pharaoh): that is, the custom of the disbelievers of Quraysh is like the custom of the folk of Pharaoh in disbelief and denial. *Da'b* means habit or custom.

*Lam yaku mughayyiran ni'mah* (He never changes a blessing): changing a blessing means replacing it with a calamity, by taking it away or by punishing its people.

*Al Fir'awn* (the folk of Pharaoh): these are all who followed his religion among the Copts, sharing with him in his wrongdoing and disbelief.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the disbelievers of Quraysh who went out from their homes wantonly and to be seen by people. Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: ﴿If you could but see when the angels take those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs﴾, and they say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾. The answer to "if" (law) is omitted, its implied meaning being (you would see a dreadful matter). His saying: ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forth, and because Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ is the speech of the angels to those among the disbelievers whom they take in death. That is: this striking and punishment is because of what your hands have sent forth of disbelief, wrongdoing, evil and corruption; and Allah, exalted is He, is not unjust to you, for He does not wrong anyone. His saying: ﴿Like the custom of the folk of Pharaoh and those before them﴾ means: the custom of these polytheists of Quraysh in their disbelief and denial is like the custom of the folk of Pharaoh and those before them, ﴿who disbelieved in the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins﴾, and these disbelievers likewise, so Allah seized them for their sins. His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong and severe in punishment﴾ is borne out by His action toward the folk of Pharaoh and those before them: 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities; and finally His seizing the disbelievers of Quraysh at Badr, the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. His saying: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ refers to the punishment He sent down upon the denying, disbelieving, wrongdoing nations, and explains His way with His servants: He, exalted is He, would not change a blessing He bestowed upon a people, such as security and ease, or purity and clarity, until they themselves change what is in themselves, by disbelieving, denying, wronging, or transgressing and committing immorality. At that point He changes those blessings into calamities: fear and scarcity take the place of security and ease, and wickedness, evil and corruption take the place of purity and clarity. This is if He does not seize them with total annihilation and complete uprooting. His saying: ﴿And that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ means: He hears the words and sees the deeds of His servants, so the recompense is completed justly, without any wrong in it. His saying: ﴿Like the custom of the folk of Pharaoh and those before them; they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins and drowned the folk of Pharaoh, and all of them were wrongdoers﴾: this verse resembles the previous one, but differs from it in the following respects. In the first, the sin for which the destroyed were seized was disbelief; in this one, it was denial. In the first, the kind of punishment was not mentioned; in the second, it was drowning. In the first, nothing was recorded against them but disbelief, which was their sin and nothing else. In the second, another sin was recorded against all of them, namely wrongdoing, when He said: ﴿and all of them were wrongdoers﴾, meaning: by their disbelief, their denial, their turning others away from the way of Allah, and their transgression against the obedience of Allah and His Messenger, with added emphasis and affirmation.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Confirmation of the punishment of the grave through the confirmation of punishment at the time of taking the soul.

2. A parallel to this verse is the verse in al-An'am: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death and the angels are extending their hands﴾ [al-An'am: 93], meaning with striking.

3. The Creator, mighty and majestic, is exalted above wronging anyone.

4. The way of Allah, exalted is He, in seizing the wrongdoers and replacing blessings with calamities.

5. It is not part of Allah's way with creation to change what people have of good or evil until they are the ones who begin it.

6. Denunciation of wrongdoing and its people, and that it is the sin which applies to all other sins.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 8, Verses 60–63**

**Explanation of the Words:**

*A'iddu* (أعدوا): prepare and make ready.

*Mastata'tum* (ما استطعتم): what you are able to.

*Min quwwah* (من قوة): that is, military strength, in terms of weapons of all kinds.

*Yuwaffa ilaykum* (يوفَّ إليكم): that is, their reward and recompense will be paid in full to you.

*Wa in janahu lil-silm* (وإن جنحوا للسلم): that is, they incline toward not fighting and desire that.

*Fa inna hasbaka Allah* (فإن حسبك الله): that is, He will suffice you against their evil and give you victory over them.

*Allafa bayna qulubihim* (ألف بين قلوبهم): that is, He united the hearts of the Ansar after they had been divided and at odds.

*Innahu 'Aziz Hakim* (إنه عزيز حكيم): that is, He prevails over His affair, and He is wise in His actions and in managing the affairs of His creation.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

These verses came in connection with the end of the Battle of Badr and the defeat of the polytheists in it. They returned to Mecca filled with rage against the believers, and Abu Sufyan indeed began preparing an army for revenge. The Battle of Uhud was nothing but a result of this. Here Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger and the believers to prepare strength and to expend whatever they can and whatever they are capable of for this purpose. So He the Exalted says: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained the "power" as archery, saying: "Indeed, the power is archery," and he said it three times. And His saying: ﴿and horses stationed [for war], by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them﴾. Allah the Exalted informs His believing servants, after commanding them to prepare strength of its various kinds, that keeping horses tethered and held in front of their homes, prepared for raiding and fighting upon them, terrifies the enemies of Allah among the disbelievers and the hypocrites, meaning it frightens them so that they will not think of invading the Muslims and fighting them. This is what is known as "armed peace," which is that when a nation is armed and capable of fighting, its enemies are terrified of it and do not wage war against it. But if they see that it has no equipment, no military supplies, and no ability to repel its enemies, that encourages them to fight it, and they do so.

His saying: ﴿and others besides them﴾ means other than the disbelieving Quraysh. His saying: ﴿whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them﴾ may refer to the Jews, the Magians, or the hypocrites, and it may also refer to the jinn. Since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not named them, it is not permissible to say definitively that they are such-and-such. Nevertheless, we know that the enemies of the Muslims are all the people of the earth who are of polytheism and disbelief, from among mankind and the jinn.

His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾ is an informing from Him, the Exalted, that whatever the Muslims spend, whether little or much, in the way of Allah, which is jihad, Allah will repay them for it in full and will not decrease any of it for them. So the clause ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾ is a clause standing independently, and its meaning is: Allah will not wrong you by diminishing the reward of your expenditures in His way. This is what the first verse [60] indicates.

As for the second verse, His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾, Allah commands His Messenger, who was the leader of jihad on that day, to accept peace whenever his enemies seek it and incline to it, desiring it sincerely, because he (ﷺ) was a messenger of mercy, not a messenger of punishment. And He commanded him to rely upon Allah in this, meaning to obey Him in accepting peace, to entrust his affair to Him, and to depend upon Him. Indeed, He the Exalted will suffice him against the evil of his enemies, because He is Hearing of their words and Knowing of their deeds and conditions; nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. Therefore He will surely suffice His Messenger against the evil of their deception, should they intend to deceive him by seeking peace and reconciliation. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, in the two verses [62] and [63]: ﴿And if they should intend to deceive you﴾, meaning by inclining toward peace and leaning toward it, ﴿then sufficient for you is Allah﴾, meaning He is your sufficiency. ﴿It is He who supported you with His help﴾, meaning at Badr, ﴿and with the believers﴾, ﴿and He brought their hearts together﴾, meaning He united those hearts that were divergent and harboring grudges and enmities, and that by the slightest and most trivial of causes. The Ansar used to live in great enmity among themselves, to the point that a war broke out between them lasting one hundred and twenty years. When they entered Islam, they reconciled, and every trace of enmity and hatred disappeared, and they became one body. Who did this other than Allah the Exalted? No one, O Allah. Therefore Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but Allah brought them together. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise﴾, meaning of wealth, both property that is still and that which moves.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The obligation of preparing strength, which in every era is according to its own measure. If in the past it was the spear, the sword, and the tethered horse, then today it is the fighter jet, the missile, the hydrogen bomb, the tank, the submarine, and the warship.

2. The establishment of the principle of "armed peace"; refer back to the explanation of the verses.

3. The Muslims will not be free of enemies as long as they are truly Muslims, because the forces of evil, from mankind and the jinn, are all hostile to them.

4. Expenditure for jihad is the best expenditure, and its multiplication is guaranteed.

5. The permissibility of accepting peace under certain conditions, and its rejection in others, according to the condition of the Muslims in strength and weakness.
