*Wa in janahu lil-silm* (وإن جنحوا للسلم): that is, they incline toward not fighting and desire that.

*Fa inna hasbaka Allah* (فإن حسبك الله): that is, He will suffice you against their evil and give you victory over them.

*Allafa bayna qulubihim* (ألف بين قلوبهم): that is, He united the hearts of the Ansar after they had been divided and at odds.

*Innahu 'Aziz Hakim* (إنه عزيز حكيم): that is, He prevails over His affair, and He is wise in His actions and in managing the affairs of His creation.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

These verses came in connection with the end of the Battle of Badr and the defeat of the polytheists in it. They returned to Mecca filled with rage against the believers, and Abu Sufyan indeed began preparing an army for revenge. The Battle of Uhud was nothing but a result of this. Here Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger and the believers to prepare strength and to expend whatever they can and whatever they are capable of for this purpose. So He the Exalted says: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) explained the "power" as archery, saying: "Indeed, the power is archery," and he said it three times. And His saying: ﴿and horses stationed [for war], by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them﴾. Allah the Exalted informs His believing servants, after commanding them to prepare strength of its various kinds, that keeping horses tethered and held in front of their homes, prepared for raiding and fighting upon them, terrifies the enemies of Allah among the disbelievers and the hypocrites, meaning it frightens them so that they will not think of invading the Muslims and fighting them. This is what is known as "armed peace," which is that when a nation is armed and capable of fighting, its enemies are terrified of it and do not wage war against it. But if they see that it has no equipment, no military supplies, and no ability to repel its enemies, that encourages them to fight it, and they do so.

His saying: ﴿and others besides them﴾ means other than the disbelieving Quraysh. His saying: ﴿whom you do not know, [but] Allah knows them﴾ may refer to the Jews, the Magians, or the hypocrites, and it may also refer to the jinn. Since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not named them, it is not permissible to say definitively that they are such-and-such. Nevertheless, we know that the enemies of the Muslims are all the people of the earth who are of polytheism and disbelief, from among mankind and the jinn.

His saying: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾ is an informing from Him, the Exalted, that whatever the Muslims spend, whether little or much, in the way of Allah, which is jihad, Allah will repay them for it in full and will not decrease any of it for them. So the clause ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾ is a clause standing independently, and its meaning is: Allah will not wrong you by diminishing the reward of your expenditures in His way. This is what the first verse [60] indicates.

As for the second verse, His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾, Allah commands His Messenger, who was the leader of jihad on that day, to accept peace whenever his enemies seek it and incline to it, desiring it sincerely, because he (ﷺ) was a messenger of mercy, not a messenger of punishment. And He commanded him to rely upon Allah in this, meaning to obey Him in accepting peace, to entrust his affair to Him, and to depend upon Him. Indeed, He the Exalted will suffice him against the evil of his enemies, because He is Hearing of their words and Knowing of their deeds and conditions; nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him. Therefore He will surely suffice His Messenger against the evil of their deception, should they intend to deceive him by seeking peace and reconciliation. This is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, in the two verses [62] and [63]: ﴿And if they should intend to deceive you﴾, meaning by inclining toward peace and leaning toward it, ﴿then sufficient for you is Allah﴾, meaning He is your sufficiency. ﴿It is He who supported you with His help﴾, meaning at Badr, ﴿and with the believers﴾, ﴿and He brought their hearts together﴾, meaning He united those hearts that were divergent and harboring grudges and enmities, and that by the slightest and most trivial of causes. The Ansar used to live in great enmity among themselves, to the point that a war broke out between them lasting one hundred and twenty years. When they entered Islam, they reconciled, and every trace of enmity and hatred disappeared, and they became one body. Who did this other than Allah the Exalted? No one, O Allah. Therefore Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but Allah brought them together. Indeed, He is Mighty and Wise﴾, meaning of wealth, both property that is still and that which moves.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The obligation of preparing strength, which in every era is according to its own measure. If in the past it was the spear, the sword, and the tethered horse, then today it is the fighter jet, the missile, the hydrogen bomb, the tank, the submarine, and the warship.

2. The establishment of the principle of "armed peace"; refer back to the explanation of the verses.

3. The Muslims will not be free of enemies as long as they are truly Muslims, because the forces of evil, from mankind and the jinn, are all hostile to them.

4. Expenditure for jihad is the best expenditure, and its multiplication is guaranteed.

5. The permissibility of accepting peace under certain conditions, and its rejection in others, according to the condition of the Muslims in strength and weakness.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 8, verses 64–66**

**Explanation of the words:**

**Hasbuka Allah** (﴿حَسْبُكَ ٱللَّهُ﴾): that is, God is sufficient for you in all that concerns you regarding your enemies and others.

**Wa man ittaba'aka mina al-mu'minin** (﴿ومَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾): that is, God is likewise sufficient for them, meaning He suffices them in all that concerns them regarding their enemies.

**Harriḍ al-mu'minin 'ala al-qital** (﴿حَرِّضِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلى ٱلْقِتالِ﴾): that is, urge them to fight, encouraging them with incentives and warnings.

**Ṣabirun** (﴿صابِرُونَ﴾): that is, in fighting, so that they do not weaken or flee, but stand firm and fight.

**La yafqahun** (﴿لاَّ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾): that is, they do not know the secrets of fighting and its outcomes, after its arts and the skill of its methods.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The Lord, blessed and exalted, addresses His Messenger by the title of prophethood with which He honored him above all people, saying ﴿O Prophet﴾. He informs him with good news, reassuring him and his followers among the believers that He is sufficient for them against their enemies, so there is nothing for them to do but fight them, as long as God, the Exalted, is their helper and supporter against them. He says: ﴿God is sufficient for you, and for those believers who follow you﴾. Then He addresses him again, saying ﴿O Prophet﴾, to command him to take up the means that bring about victory by God's permission, which is to urge the believers to fight, to encourage them to it, and to make them desire it. He says ﴿Urge the believers to fight﴾. He informs him, commanding him and his believing followers, that ﴿if there are among you twenty steadfast ones﴾, that is, if there are among them in the battle, ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾. And if there are among them one hundred steadfast ones, they will overcome a thousand of the disbelievers. He gives the reason for this, saying ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾, that is, the disbelievers do not understand the secrets of fighting. These secrets are that God is worshiped, that injustice is removed from the earth, and that God takes believers as martyrs and grants them the ranks of martyrs with Him. The disbelievers do not understand this, which is why they do not endure fighting, since they fight only for the sake of their lives. So when they fear for their lives, they abandon the fight, seeking a life beyond that. Moreover, they are ignorant and do not know the methods of war or its effective means. This is unlike the believers, who are knowledgeable, knowledgeable in everything. This is what is expected. If faith weakens, knowledge and understanding weaken along with it, and ignorance and weakness take hold, as is observed today among Muslims.

As for His saying, ﴿Now God has lightened your burden, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred steadfast ones, they will overcome two hundred, and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two thousand, by God's permission. And God is with the steadfast﴾: now, after God's knowledge of your weakness, since one person cannot withstand ten, nor ten a hundred, nor a hundred a thousand, God has lightened the burden out of mercy toward you and as a favor to you. He thereby abrogated the first ruling with the second, which is that one may fight two, ten may fight twenty, a hundred may fight two hundred, and a thousand may fight two thousand. The implication is that a believer may not flee from two, but may flee if they are more than two. The same applies to the other ratios: ten are forbidden to flee from twenty, but they may flee from thirty or forty, for example. This is only a matter of removing hardship. Otherwise, it is permissible for a believer to fight ten or more. Three thousand Companions fought a hundred and fifty thousand from the Byzantines and the Arab Christians at the Battle of Mu'tah. His saying ﴿by God's permission﴾ means by His aid and support, since there is no victory without God's help and permission. His saying ﴿And God is with the steadfast﴾ means with support and victory. Patience is a condition for God's support and aid, so whoever does not persevere in fighting has no promise from God of His victory and support.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. There is no sufficient one but God, the Exalted. Whoever claims that there is someone other than God who suffices is guilty of shirk (associating partners with God).

2. It is obligatory to urge the believers to jihad and to encourage them to it at every time and place.

3. It is forbidden for one to flee from one, or for two to flee from one, and it is permissible for numbers beyond that.

4. It is obligatory to train the fighters intellectually, spiritually, and in military skill (ṣinā'ah).

5. Steadfastness in the battlefield is obligatory, and fleeing is forbidden when the number of believers is twelve thousand fighters or more, since such a number will not be overcome through lack of numbers, by God's permission.

6. God's companionship, through knowledge, support, and victory, belongs to the steadfast, not to the fainthearted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 67–69:

Explanation of the words:

Asra (prisoners): plural of asir (prisoner), who is one taken in war and customarily bound with an isar, a leather fetter. The word asir was then applied to anyone taken in war.

Hatta yuthkhina fi al-ardh (until he has established dominance in the land): that is, he has strength and power by which he inspires fear in the enemy.

Arad al-dunya (the goods of this world): that is, wealth, because it is passing and will vanish without remaining.

Lawla kitab min Allah sabaq (Were it not for a decree from Allah that had preceded): this is the Book of Destinies, by which Allah the Exalted had made the spoils of war lawful for the Prophet of this community.

Fima akhadhtum (for what you took): that is, because of the ransom you took for the prisoners of Badr.

Halalan tayyiban (lawful and good): the lawful is the good, so the word tayyiban is an emphasis on the lawfulness that the context required.

Wattaqu Allah (fear Allah): that is, by obeying Him and obeying His Messenger in what he commands and forbids.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns the events of the Battle of Badr. The Companions of the Messenger ﷺ, except Umar and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (may Allah be pleased with them both), desired to ransom the prisoners with wealth because of the harsh living conditions they were enduring. Their desire for ransom was without knowledge from Allah of whether it was permitted or forbidden. As for Umar, he would not find a prisoner without killing him. As for Sa'd, he said: "Establishing dominance in battle is better than sparing men." When the ransom was completed, this noble verse was revealed rebuking them with the sharpest rebuke. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿It is not for a Prophet﴾, that is, it is not proper for him, nor was it fitting for him, to have prisoners of war whom he keeps in order to ransom them or to grant them freedom without payment ﴿until he has established dominance in the land﴾, the land of the enemy, by killing and dispersing them. When he is known for might and firmness and the enemies stand in awe of him, then it is permitted for him to take prisoners, that is, to keep the prisoners alive so that he may grant them freedom without compensation or ransom them for wealth. As for His saying, ﴿You desire the goods of this world﴾, this is part of His rebuke to them, since they ransomed the prisoners only because they desired the trifles of this world, which is wealth. And His saying, ﴿but Allah desires the Hereafter﴾: how vast is the difference between your desire and the desire of your Lord for you. You desire the passing goods, while Allah desires for you the lasting bliss. And His saying, ﴿And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾, that is, Dominant over His affair, He grants victory to whoever relies upon Him and entrusts his affair to Him, and Wise in His dispositions, so He does not forsake His allies or grant victory to His enemies. So you, O believers, must seek His good pleasure by abandoning what you desire in favor of what He desires, glory be to Him and exalted. And His saying, ﴿Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had preceded, you would have been touched for what you took by a great punishment﴾, that is, had it not been that Allah's knowledge of the lawfulness of the spoils for this community had already passed and had been written in the Preserved Tablet, there would have befallen you, for your approval of ransoming and taking the ransom, a great punishment.

And His saying, ﴿So eat of what you have gained, lawful and good﴾: this is permission from Him, the Exalted, to the people of Badr to eat of what they gained, including what they ransomed the prisoners with, and it is a favor from Him, glory be to Him and exalted. And His saying, ﴿And fear Allah﴾: a command from Him, Mighty and Majestic, to fear Him by carrying out His commands and those of His Messenger and abstaining from their prohibitions. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: an announcement from Him, the Exalted, that He is forgiving toward whoever of His servants repents and merciful toward the believers among them. This was manifested in the lifting of punishment from them, as He forgave them and permitted them what they had desired and wanted.

And in the hadith: "Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you."

Guidance from the verses:

1- Allah's instruction to the leaders of the Islamic nation in jihad: they should not ransom prisoners, nor grant them release as a favor, until they have established dominance in the enemy's land by killing and dispersing them. When the enemy fears and stands in awe of them, then they may ransom the prisoners or grant them release.

2- Discouraging desire for this world because of its worthlessness, and encouraging the Hereafter because of its great reward.

3- The permissibility of spoils of war.

4- The obligation to fear Allah by obeying Him and His Messenger in what they command and forbid.

Arad al-dunya (the goods of this world): that is, wealth, because it is passing and will vanish without remaining.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 70–71:

Explanation of the words:

Among the captives: the captives of Badr from whom ransom was taken, such as al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him.

If Allah knows any good in your hearts: that is, sincere faith and complete sincerity.

Of what has been taken from you: of the ransom wealth.

And if they intend treachery against you: that is, the captives.

Then they had already betrayed Allah before: that is, before they fell into captivity, by their disbelief in Makkah.

So He gave you power over them: that is, He enabled you, the believers, over them, so you killed them and took them captive.

And Allah is Knowing, Wise: Knowing of His creation, Wise in His making and His management.

The meaning of the two verses:

These noble verses were revealed concerning al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him, as he used to say: "This verse was revealed concerning me." That is because, after he fell into captivity, he embraced Islam and made his Islam apparent, and he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to return to him the ransom that had been taken from him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused him that, so Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to those captives in your hands: If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾, that is, true Islam, ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾, that is, better wealth, ﴿and will forgive you﴾ your sins, which were disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, and then warfare against Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving﴾, He forgives the sins of His repentant servants, ﴿Merciful﴾ to His believing servants, so He does not take them to account for those sins after repentance, but shows them mercy in this world and the Hereafter. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But if they intend treachery against you﴾, that is: if these captives, from whom ransom was taken, and who uttered the two testimonies, showing their Islam, intend to betray you and deceive you by displaying Islam, and then when they return to their homelands they return to their disbelief, then do not concern yourselves with them and do not fear their side, for they had already betrayed Allah before by their disbelief and their polytheism. ﴿So He gave power over them﴾ to the believers, placing them in their grasp and under their command. And had they returned, Allah the Exalted would have returned to empower you over them and enable you against them. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, that is, Knowing of the intentions of the people and their movements, Wise in what He decrees concerning them. So let them fear Him, the Mighty and Majestic, let them make their Islam good and be sincere in their faith, for that is better for them.

Guidance from the two verses:

From the guidance of the two verses:

1- The virtue of al-'Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, since the verse was revealed concerning his case and affair.

2- The virtue of harboring good and righteous intentions.

3- The application of the word "good" to Islam and the Qur'an, and both are truly good, and all good.

4- No servant leaves anything for Allah except that He compensates him with something better than it.

5- Allah, the Majestic: no conqueror overcomes Him and no fugitive escapes Him. So let him fear Him and rely upon Him.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 8, verses 72–75:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Amanu* (آمنوا): they affirmed Allah and His Messenger, believed in meeting Allah, and affirmed His promise and His warning.

*Wa-haajaru* (وهاجروا): that is, they left their homes and joined the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the city of Madinah.

*Fi sabili Allah* (في سبيل الله): that is, for the sake of worshipping Allah alone and not associating anything else with Him, which is Islam.

*Aawaw* (آووا): that is, they sheltered the emigrants, took them into their homes, and supported them against their enemies.

*Wa-in istansarukum* (وإن استنصروكم): that is, they asked you for help against their enemies.

*Mithaq* (ميثاق): a covenant, that is, a treaty of peace and non-aggression.

*Illa tafAAluhu* (إلاَّ تفعلوه): that is, if you do not ally with the Muslims and sever ties with the disbelievers, there will be fitnah (civil strife, trial and tumult).

*Ulu al-arham* (أولوا الأرحام): that is, relatives by blood.

*Ba'duhum awla bi-ba'd* (بعضهم أولى ببعض): in inheritance, that is, some of them inherit from others.

**The meaning of the verses:**

On the occasion of concluding the account of the events of the Battle of Badr al-Kubra, Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the condition of the believers during that period, and that they differ in perfection. So He, whose word is truth, said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah﴾. This is one category: its people combined faith, emigration, and jihad with wealth and life. The second category is in His words: ﴿And those who gave shelter and helped﴾, that is, they sheltered the Messenger (ﷺ) and the emigrants in their homes and supported them. These are the two categories of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and they are the most perfect of the believers and the highest in rank. They will be mentioned again at the end of the passage, so that their reward with their Lord may be stated. His words about them, ﴿Those are allies of one another﴾, mean in support, alliance, and inheritance. However, inheritance was abrogated by His words at the end of this passage ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another﴾.

The third category of believers is mentioned in His words: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate﴾, that is, they believed in Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Day, but then were content to remain among the disbelievers, and did not emigrate from their homes and wealth to join the abode of emigration in the Prophet's city of Madinah. These are deficient in their faith by their abandonment of emigration. Allah says concerning them to His Messenger and the believers: ﴿You have no obligation of guardianship toward them at all﴾. So there is no inheritance and no alliance requiring support and love until they emigrate to you and join you. Allah makes an exception for them, a special case: if they ask the believers for help in religion, it is incumbent upon the believers to help them, on condition that the one who has wronged and harmed them, for whose sake they seek help, is not someone with whom the believers have a treaty of peace and abstention from war. In that case, the believers must fulfill their covenant and not betray it, and so they must not help those who sit back from emigration. This is what is indicated by His words: ﴿And if they seek help from you in religion, then you must help, except against a people between you and whom there is a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. He concluded the statement with this sentence to inform both the perfect and the deficient believers that Allah is aware of their conduct and knowing of their deeds and circumstances, so let them be mindful of Him in this, lest they step outside His obedience.

His words in verse [73]: ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾, that is, they support one another and inherit from one another. Based on this, He says: ﴿If you do not do it, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, that is, if you do not do what you were commanded: allying with the believers in love, support, and loyalty, and opposing the disbelievers through hatred, abandonment, and warfare against them, there will be a great fitnah whose extent cannot be measured and a great corruption whose limit cannot be known. Fitnah is polytheism, and corruption is sins.

His words in verse [74]: ﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped—those are the believers in truth﴾. This is the first category, mentioned again so that its reward with its Lord may be stated after establishing and confirming their faith. So He said concerning them: ﴿Those are the believers in truth. For them is forgiveness﴾, that is, for their sins, by covering them and not holding them accountable for them, ﴿and provision generous﴾, which is the bliss of Paradise in the proximity of their Lord, glory be to Him and exalted.

The fourth category of believers is mentioned by Him in His words: ﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove with you—those are of you﴾. This category is more perfect than the third and less than the first and second, since the first and second won the precedence, while these came after them. But because of their faith, emigration, and jihad, Allah joined them to the foremost, saying: ﴿Those are of you﴾. His words ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another﴾ mean in inheritance, and by it the inheritance through emigration and pact was abrogated, and inheritance became established through kinship, marriage, and clientage, and through lineage until the Day of Resurrection. His words ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ mean in His judgment and decree recorded in the Preserved Tablet. His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ — this sentence is a conclusion encompassing both promise and warning: the promise is for the people of faith and obedience, and the warning is for the people of polytheism and sins.

**Guidance from the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Clarification of the variation among believers in their perfections and the elevation of their ranks before their Lord.

2. The most perfect believers are those who combined faith, emigration, and jihad and took precedence in that; they are the early Emigrants, and those who combined faith, sheltering, support, and jihad, who are the Helpers (Ansar).

3. Below them are those who believed, emigrated, and strove, but after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah.

4. And the least of the categories of believers are those who believed but did not emigrate; these are in great peril.

5. The obligation to support the believers through loyalty and love, and the obligation to oppose the disbelievers, abandon them, and hold enmity toward them.

6. The abrogation of inheritance through anything other than marriage, kinship, and clientage.

This is what is indicated by His words: ﴿And if they seek help from you in religion, then you must help, except against a people between you and whom there is a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. He concluded the statement with this sentence to inform both the perfect and the deficient believers that Allah is aware of their conduct and knowing of their deeds and circumstances, so let them be mindful of Him in this, lest they step outside His obedience.

His words in verse [73]: ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾, that is, they support one another and inherit from one another. Based on this, He says: ﴿If you do not do it, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾, that is, if you do not do what you were commanded: allying with the believers in love, support, and loyalty, and opposing the disbelievers through hatred, abandonment, and warfare against them, there will be a great fitnah whose extent cannot be measured and a great corruption whose limit cannot be known. Fitnah is polytheism, and corruption is sins.

His words in verse [74]: ﴿And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and helped—those are the believers in truth﴾. This is the first category, mentioned again so that its reward with its Lord may be stated after establishing and confirming their faith. So He said concerning them: ﴿Those are the believers in truth. For them is forgiveness﴾, that is, for their sins, by covering them and not holding them accountable for them, ﴿and provision generous﴾, which is the bliss of Paradise in the proximity of their Lord, glory be to Him and exalted.

The fourth category of believers is mentioned by Him in His words: ﴿And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove with you—those are of you﴾. This category is more perfect than the third and less than the first and second, since the first and second won the precedence, while these came after them. But because of their faith, emigration, and jihad, Allah joined them to the foremost, saying: ﴿Those are of you﴾. His words ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another﴾ mean in inheritance, and by it the inheritance through emigration and pact was abrogated, and inheritance became established through kinship, marriage, and clientage, and through lineage until the Day of Resurrection. His words ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ mean in His judgment and decree recorded in the Preserved Tablet. His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ — this sentence is a conclusion encompassing both promise and warning: the promise is for the people of faith and obedience, and the warning is for the people of polytheism and sins.

**Guidance from the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. Clarification of the variation among believers in their perfections and the elevation of their ranks before their Lord.

2. The most perfect believers are those who combined faith, emigration, and jihad and took precedence in that; they are the early Emigrants, and those who combined faith, sheltering, support, and jihad, who are the Helpers (Ansar).

3. Below them are those who believed, emigrated, and strove, but after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah.

4. And the least of the categories of believers are those who believed but did not emigrate; these are in great peril.

5. The obligation to support the believers through loyalty and love, and the obligation to oppose the disbelievers, abandon them, and hold enmity toward them.

6. The abrogation of inheritance through anything other than marriage, kinship, and clientage.

*Fi sabili Allah* (في سبيل الله): that is, for the sake of worshipping Allah alone and not associating anything else with Him, which is Islam.

*Aawaw* (آووا): that is, they sheltered the emigrants, took them into their homes, and supported them against their enemies.

*Wa-in istansarukum* (وإن استنصروكم): that is, they asked you for help against their enemies.

*Mithaq* (ميثاق): a covenant, that is, a treaty of peace and non-aggression.
